newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy court says no Priebke extradition to Germany.
newsitem.headline: Italy court says no Priebke extradition to Germany.

text.p: Italy's constitutional court has ruled that former Nazi SS Captain Erich Priebke, accused of wartime atrocity, cannot be extradited to Germany because he is facing the same charges in Rome.
The court cited a 1957 European convention on extradition for its decision, which was made on February 14 but only made public on Monday.

The 83-year-old former Nazi is accused of complicity in multiple murder for his role in the massacre of 335 men and boys at the Ardeatine Caves near Rome on March 24, 1944. Seventy-five of the victims were Jews.
At his first trial last August, a military court found Priebke guilty but ordered him freed, citing extenuating circumstances which triggered an expired statute of limitations.
Citing a German extradition request, Italian justice officials ordered him rearrested that night after relatives of the massacre's victims laid siege to the courthouse.
The August verdict was quashed on appeal in October.

Last month the Court of Cassation, Italy's highest court, ruled that a military tribunal should hear Priebke's re-trial instead of a civilian court as families of the victims had wanted. A date for the new military trial has not been set.
Priebke is being held in detention at a military prison in Rome. He has been jailed since November 1995 when he was extradited from Argentina, where he had lived openly since 1948.
Priebke admits shooting two victims and crossing names off a list but said he had to follow orders or be killed himself.
He also says the massacre was a legitimate wartime reprisal for a partisans' bomb attack in Rome the previous day which killed 33 soldiers loyal to Nazi occupying forces.
